nodes.description: Growth plate histology shows slightly enlarged chondrocytes and hypercellularity, with hypercellularity of the reserve zone and round resting chondrocytes, while column formation in the proliferative and hypertrophic zones is relatively preserved. This preserved column architecture is one of the histological features that separate the Torrance type from thanatophoric dysplasia; focal disruption of columns has been seen in some cases.

nodes.description: A heterozygous variant in the exons encoding the C-propeptide of the pro-alpha1(II) chain: missense changes, in-frame deletions, and nonsense or frameshift changes in the last exon that are expected to escape nonsense-mediated decay. The variant allele is translated into an altered chain rather than acting as a null allele, which is why the variants are considered dominant negative.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant negative mutations in the C-propeptide of COL2A1 cause platyspondylic lethal skeletal dysplasia, torrance type, and define a novel subfamily within the type 2 collagenopathies.
evidence.snippet: We studied eight additional cases of PLSD-T and found that all had mutations in the C-propeptide domain of COL2A1. The mutational spectrum includes missense, stop codon and frameshift mutations. All non-sense mutations were located in the last exon, where they would escape non-sense-mediated RNA-decay.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant negative mutations in the C-propeptide of COL2A1 cause platyspondylic lethal skeletal dysplasia, torrance type, and define a novel subfamily within the type 2 collagenopathies.
